title: automerge 0.5.0
description: Closes #49.

title: Build bundled library with Cargo directly, drop CMake
description:
## Summary

CMake was only orchestrating Cargo in the bundled build. For this package its essential jobs were (1) substituting the `Cargo.toml`/`cbindgen.toml` templates and (2) running `cargo build` (where `build.rs` runs cbindgen to emit the header) plus two textual fix-ups to that header. Everything else CMake did — `config.h`, enum-string codegen, compiling the C `utils/` sources, and merging static archives — produces artifacts this package never uses (the merge folds C utility objects we don't link).

This PR removes the CMake dependency:

- **`configure` / `configure.win`**: replace the CMake invocation with a direct `cargo build --release`, then reproduce the two header fix-ups CMake applied via `sed`:
  - `A_M…` → `AM_…` (cbindgen renders consecutive capitals with a stray underscore)
  - `USIZE_` → pointer size (cbindgen ignores `size_of::<usize>()`), read from `.Machine$sizeof.pointer`
  - stage `libautomerge_core.a` as `am-install/lib/libautomerge.a`. The install layout is unchanged, so **Makevars need no edits**.
- **tools workflow**: `tools/patch-sources.sh` now generates `Cargo.toml` and `cbindgen.toml` from the upstream `cmake/*.in` templates (as CMake's `configure_file` did) and removes `CMakeLists.txt` + `cmake/`, instead of patching `CMakeLists.txt`. The obsolete `CMakeLists.txt` patches are dropped from `patch-rust-msrv.sh` and `vendor-deps.sh`.
- **bundled tree**: `CMakeLists.txt` and `cmake/` removed (the generated TOMLs are already tracked).
- **`SystemRequirements`**: drop `CMake >= 3.25`; Rust (Cargo + `rustc >= 1.85`) is now the only build toolchain. README, vignette, NEWS, and `cleanup` updated.

Net: **+129 / −1247 lines**, one fewer system dependency.

title: Simplify `am_text_update()` API
description:
Remove the `old_text` parameter from `am_text_update()`. The current text content is now read directly from the document in C, so callers only need to pass the new text:                                                     

```r                                                                            
# Before                                                                  
old_text <- am_text_content(text_obj)
am_text_update(text_obj, old_text, "Hello World")

# After
am_text_update(text_obj, "Hello World")
```
 
This is a breaking change to the function signature. The `old_text` argument was redundant since the text object already carries a reference back to its parent document.

title: Expose more automerge-c functionality
description:
## Summary

Add 16 new functions (C + R) exposing additional automerge-c capabilities: document cloning/equality, incremental save/load, pending ops, empty changes, conflict inspection (get-all), range queries, object item introspection, missing dependency checks, document decomposition into changes, mark clearing, and sync state serialization.

## New Functions

**Document operations** (`document.c` / `document.R`):
- `am_clone()` — deep copy a document (preserves actor ID; for archival/snapshots)
- `am_equal()` — test two documents for state equality
- `am_pending_ops()` — count uncommitted operations
- `am_commit_empty()` — create an empty change for bookkeeping
- `am_save_incremental()` — save only changes since last save
- `am_load_incremental()` — apply incremental changes to a document

**Object operations** (`objects.c` / `objects.R`):
- `am_map_get_all()` — get all conflicting values for a map key
- `am_list_get_all()` — get all conflicting values at a list index
- `am_map_range()` — get a range of map entries by key
- `am_list_range()` — get a subrange of list items by index
- `am_items()` — get all key-value entries from any object

**Change/sync operations** (`sync.c`, `changes.c` / `sync.R`):
- `am_get_missing_deps()` — check document completeness
- `am_load_changes()` — decompose saved document bytes into individual changes

**Mark operations** (`cursors.c` / `cursors.R`):
- `am_mark_clear()` — remove a mark from a text range

**Sync serialization** (`sync.c` / `sync.R`):
- `am_sync_state_encode()` — serialize sync state to bytes
- `am_sync_state_decode()` — restore sync state from bytes

title: Implement change introspection, cursor serialization and time travel capability
description:
- New `am_change_*()` functions for extracting metadata (hash, message, time, actor ID, sequence number, deps) and serializing changes to/from bytes                                                                     
- Change-returning functions now return `am_change()` objects instead of raw vectors
- New cursor serialization `am_cursor_to_bytes/string()`, `am_cursor_from_bytes/string()` and comparison `am_cursor_equal()`
- `am_cursor()`, `am_cursor_position()`, `am_marks()`, `am_marks_at()` gain `heads` parameter for historical state queries
- Rename `am_sync_state_new()` to `am_sync_state()` for API consistency

title: Implement uint64 type
description:
Closes #7.

## Problem

When uint64 values are read from automerge documents (created by other language bindings like JavaScript or Python), they lose their type information when converted to R's double. When written back to the document, they become f64 instead of uint64, breaking type fidelity across language bindings.

## Solution

Follow the existing `am_counter` pattern: use S3 classes to preserve type information through the round-trip.

title: automerge-c: fix MRI script
description:
Follow up to #3, which inadvertently broke MacOS builds.

This PR is a solution Claude Code provides as a fallback, as GNU ar's MRI (Machine Readable Interface) mode with the -M flag is not supported by BSD ar (the default on macOS).

title: automerge-c: remove rust-toolchain.toml, patch CMakeLists.txt to use MRI script for GNU ar
description:
This PR lets the package build on Windows.

Thanks @eitsupi for identifying that the presence of `rust-toolchain.toml` would cause rustup to install a new toolchain over the existing one, which is where the build was stalling on CI.

Removal of that file unblocked the build, which then failed at the linking stage. Claude Code correctly diagnosed the failure to the below issue and found a workable solution using a GNU ar MRI (Machine Readable Interface) script. (We cause the fallback to ar by avoiding the MSVC lib tool in c49b1c4)

`${CMAKE_AR} -rs $<TARGET_FILE_NAME:${LIBRARY_NAME}> ${BINDINGS_OBJECTS_DIR}/*.o`
> 
>   On Windows with MinGW's ar.exe from Rtools45, this wildcard is not being expanded
>   properly because:
>   1. Windows ar.exe doesn't expand wildcards like Unix shells do
>   2. CMake executes this command directly without shell expansion
>   3. The literal string objects/automerge_core/*.o is being passed to ar, which
>   interprets it as a non-existent file path

title: Fix build on Windows ARM64
description:
This fixes the build on Windows ARM64.

Before: https://github.com/r-universe/cran/actions/runs/30698875488/attempts/1
After: https://github.com/r-universe/cran/actions/runs/30698875488/job/91416921620

When cross-compiling (Windows arm64 sets `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm`), cargo nests the artifact under `am-build/target/<triple>/release`, so staging from `am-build/target/release` fails. This looks in the target-specific subdirectory when `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` is set.

For more details see https://github.com/r-devel/windows-arm64
